title: Week of Nov 9
text: Written Nov 2 from LinkedIn and Instagram posts published Oct 19 to Nov 1 (Supermetrics): 26 LinkedIn posts, the last on Oct 30, and 21 Instagram posts, the last on Oct 31. Compared with Sep 21 to Oct 18 and with September. Series and partners come from the ATM Kitchen board, refreshed Nov 2. Last week's two experiments run Nov 2 to 6, so their results come next week.

title: On LinkedIn, an off-duty cut built on one personal habit drew the most reach, and generic seasonal cuts drew the least.
text: Jill Kelly (Assembly) on 15 years of carving pumpkins drew 3,243 impressions and 28 comments on Oct 28, the most of any LinkedIn post Oct 19 to Nov 1, against a median guest post of 845. Six off-duty cuts on one habit since Sep 15 (Kelly, plus KC Sullivan's martini, Lori Goode's interpretive dance, Nicolas Bidon's cooking, Liz Jenkins's SNL slumber parties and Rich DiGeronimo's marathons) have a median of 2,240, while the four generic fall cuts since Sep 22 (Baker Machado, Will McIntosh, Meredith Diehn, Elizabeth Latham) have a median of 153. Latham's fall cut drew 239 six days after her Marriott Media interview drew 1,916, and Machado's drew 173 four weeks after his only other post, so the guest is not the problem: the style guide's rule that specific beats general is. A light topic is not enough on its own: Nayeema Raza on polka dots drew 108.

title: Instagram guest reels more than doubled their reach in the first week of the collab test.
text: The eight single-guest reels of Oct 26 to Nov 1 reached a median 570 accounts, against 223 for the six of Oct 19 to 25 and 312 for the 26 of Sep 21 to Oct 18; five of the eight passed 500, and none of the six the week before did. Alice Ma (Mad Realities) reached 1,214, Andrew Almendras (IMAX) 982 with 131 likes and 20 comments, and Amanda Forrester's reel (OpenX) drew 24 shares, the most of any reel since Oct 6. Instagram's 28-day reach rose from 26,803 (to Oct 26) to 28,114 (to Nov 1), after falling at every reading since Sep 24, though it is still 35% below the 28 days to Sep 24. The two that lagged were Diana Haussling's second honoree reel (206) and Jill Kelly's (281). The data does not show which reels were accepted collabs, so check that in Instagram before crediting the test.

title: On Instagram, opening on a number or fact has not lifted reach, and career-story openers did better in each of the last two weeks.
text: The style guide asks Instagram first lines to give one repeatable fact or number. Of the 14 guest reels Oct 19 to Nov 1, the five that opened on a number or fact reached a median 281 (Juan Camilo Arjona Ferreira 165, Barbara Peng 225, Jill Kelly 281, Amanda Forrester 502, Michelle Crossan-Matos 730), and the five that opened on a career story reached 475 (Todd Porch 213, Rachel Oppenheim 285, Caitlin Coburn Winsor 475, Keri Richardson 517, Andrew Almendras 982). The gap held in both weeks: 195 against 285 for Oct 19 to 25, and 502 against 750 for Oct 26 to Nov 1. The two contrast openers also did well (Alice Ma 1,214, Nayeema Raza 623), while October's best fact opener, Andrea Hopelain's "23,000 NFL seasons" (2,401 on Oct 8), was an accepted WPP Media collab. The samples are small, so the rule is unproven rather than wrong.

title: Post one off-duty cut on a single personal habit, and no generic seasonal cut.
text: In the week of Nov 9, post one Masterclass Off Duty or other off-duty cut on LinkedIn, Tuesday to Thursday in the main slot, as the only guest cut that day. Pick a guest who has not been on the feed since Oct 9, and build the first line on their own habit or tradition, with a number if there is one, as the Jill Kelly post did ("For 15 years, she and her family have carved..."). Name the guest's title and company and tag both. Hold any generic holiday or season cut (Thanksgiving, fall, back to work) until a guest gives a personal story to hang it on.
next_step: Measure: impressions after seven days against 845, the median LinkedIn guest post Oct 19 to Nov 1 (2,240, the median of six habit cuts since Sep 15, is the stretch), and comments against 28 (Jill Kelly, Oct 28).

title: Split next week's guest reels between fact openers and career-story openers.
text: For the guest reels of Nov 9 to 13 (four or more), write two first lines for each: one repeatable fact or number, as the style guide asks, and one career story ("How a Spanish degree led him around the world before arriving at IMAX."). Post them alternately, starting with a fact opener, and keep the rest of each caption the same: "[Name] at @company on why ...", the handles, and "Watch the full conversation through the link in our profile." Send the collab invite to the guest and the company on every reel, so the opener is the only difference, and keep a list of which opener each reel used.
next_step: Measure: median reach per opener after seven days, both against 570 (guest reels Oct 26 to Nov 1); fact openers had a median of 281 and career-story openers 475 over Oct 19 to Nov 1.
